history.headline: Eight days to the crossing and the taper is fully engaged. Legs are banked, strength held to the last, and the quiet is deliberate. The audit begins when the trail does.
watch_items: Watch how the legs respond to the shift from short controlled runs to sustained daily time-on-feet in the crossing's first two or three days — that's the real durability audit.
Note whether strength holds one final light session or goes to zero in the last pre-travel days; either is fine, just track which way it breaks.
Keep an eye on whether step activity stays warm through the packing-and-travel window rather than collapsing entirely as logistics intensify.
Once the crossing begins, watch how easy-run HR behaves under pack load and cumulative fatigue — the first sustained days will reset what "easy" costs.

history.headline: Taper is complete and the engine is intact. Two runs today, both easy, HR obedient. From here it's travel and logistics — the crossing writes the next chapter.
watch_items: Watch how easy-run HR responds once daily pack-loaded efforts stack up — the first few days will reset what "easy" actually costs.
Note whether steps hold through the packing-and-travel window or collapse as logistics peak, as a read on residual movement into the transition.
Track back-to-back leg response over the opening days of the crossing — early durability under cumulative load is the genuine unknown, not fitness.
Keep an eye on whether recovery steadies before departure, given how variable recent nights have looked heading into a sustained demand.

history.headline: Six days out from the crossing, the taper has landed clean. Legs are banked, engine intact, movement holding through the logistics window. The next chapter is written on the trail, not here.
watch_items: Watch whether recovery nights steady in the final days before departure — this is the one metric that's stayed variable and the one that compounds most under a multi-day self-supported load.
Once the crossing begins, track how easy-run HR responds to daily pack-loaded efforts stacking up — the first two or three days will redefine what "easy" actually costs.
Note the back-to-back leg response over the opening stretch; early durability under cumulative load is the genuine unknown, not the underlying fitness.
Keep an eye on whether movement holds through the final travel window as a read on residual freshness into the transition.

history.headline: Five days to the crossing. The taper has held clean and the final travel window is here. Everything from now is logistics — the trail writes the rest.
watch_items: Watch whether recovery nights finally steady through the travel-and-transition days — it's been the one persistently variable thread and the one that compounds most once daily pack-loaded efforts stack up.
Over the opening stretch, note how "easy" HR responds as consecutive loaded days accumulate — the first few days will redefine what easy actually costs.
Track the back-to-back leg response early; cumulative durability under a 6-8kg pack is the genuine unknown, not the underlying engine.
Once the trail begins, watch how the mountain-crossing section sits within the daily rhythm — the border climb is the one terrain spike worth reading separately from the flatter days.

history.headline: Four days out and the final quiet holds. Strength stayed live right up to the edge, legs are fresh, engine banked. Everything from here is the trail itself.
watch_items: Watch how "easy" HR behaves once consecutive loaded days begin — the first few days will reset what easy actually costs under a pack.
Track the back-to-back leg response early; cumulative durability under load is still the real unknown, not the engine.
Note how the border mountain crossing sits within the daily rhythm — read that terrain spike separately from the flatter sections.
Watch whether recovery nights steady once the trail rhythm replaces the travel-and-logistics window.
